chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Sayyari, from Abu Ali ibn Rashid, raised it from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), when he did not have a sauce (udm) for him, would cut the bread with the knife.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)
key_terms.أُدْمٌ: Sauce, side dish, or condiment eaten with bread

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali do when he did not have a side dish with his bread?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the asceticism (zuhd) of Imam Ali (AS), showing that his simplicity was not merely about scarcity but a deliberate choice to avoid luxury even when resources were available. By cutting bread with a knife in the absence of a side dish, he demonstrated that the act of eating is a functional necessity rather than a source of indulgence, a trait highly valued in Shia ethical teachings. This practice underscores the principle that dignity lies in contentment with basic sustenance rather than in elaborate culinary accompaniments.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Sayyari, from Abu Ali Bin Rashid, 
(It has been narrated) raising it from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>, whenever he<sup>asws</sup> did not have a sauce for him<sup>asws</sup>, cut the bread with the knife’.
en.sarwar: 9. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Sayyariy from abu Ali ibn Rashid in a marfu‘ manner has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
when ’Amir al-Mu’minin did not have curry; he would cut the bread with a knife.’”
